counties.name: Mecklenburg County
counties.summary: Selke Pest Control provides residential general pest control, mosquito control, flea and tick control, and rodent control throughout Mecklenburg County, North Carolina, including Charlotte, Huntersville, Cornelius, Davidson, and Matthews.
counties.geography: Mecklenburg County is the most urbanized county in the Charlotte region, but it is also one of the most pest-active. Lake Norman borders the county to the north, Mountain Island Lake and the Catawba River form its western edge, and greenway creek corridors such as Little Sugar Creek, McAlpine Creek, Mallard Creek, and Torrence Creek run directly through residential neighborhoods. Those creek buffers and the county's large tree canopy hold humidity and shade, which is why mosquitoes, ticks, and moisture-loving pests stay active from early spring through late fall.
pests: Asian tiger mosquitoes and Culex mosquitoes along creeks and retention ponds
Lone star, American dog, and black-legged ticks on wooded lot lines
Fire ants in new-construction lawns and common areas
American and German cockroaches in denser neighborhoods
House mice and roof rats entering homes in fall and winter

faqs.q: Does Selke Pest Control serve all of Mecklenburg County?
faqs.a: Yes. We serve residential properties across Mecklenburg County, including Charlotte, Huntersville, Cornelius, Davidson, and Matthews, along with surrounding unincorporated communities. Call 704-728-0204 to confirm service for your address.

faqs.q: When is mosquito season in Mecklenburg County?
faqs.a: Mosquito activity in Mecklenburg County typically runs from late March or April through October, peaking from June through August. Monthly barrier treatments during the warm season provide the most consistent protection.

faqs.q: How much does pest control cost in Mecklenburg County?
faqs.a: Pricing depends on home size, lot size, and the pests involved. Selke Pest Control provides free quotes by phone at 704-728-0204 or through the online quote form, and every quarterly plan includes the Selke Guarantee for free re-treatments between visits.

counties.name: Iredell County
counties.summary: Selke Pest Control is headquartered in Mooresville and provides residential pest control throughout Iredell County, North Carolina, including Mooresville, Statesville, and Troutman.
counties.geography: Iredell County stretches from the northern shoreline of Lake Norman up through the Piedmont foothills. Southern Iredell, including Mooresville and the Brawley School Road peninsula, has hundreds of miles of lakefront coves that create extended mosquito seasons. Central and northern Iredell, including Troutman and Statesville, mix farmland, wooded creeks such as Fifth Creek and Third Creek, and fast-growing subdivisions, which drives tick, fire ant, and rodent pressure.
pests: Mosquitoes along Lake Norman coves and shoreline properties
Ticks on wooded and rural acreage
Fire ants in open lawns and new subdivisions
Carpenter ants in older and moisture-damaged structures
Mice and rats moving in from farmland in the fall

faqs.q: Is Selke Pest Control based in Iredell County?
faqs.a: Yes. Selke Pest Control is a family-owned company based in Mooresville, in southern Iredell County, which lets us offer fast scheduling and same-day service availability for Iredell County homeowners.

faqs.q: Which Iredell County towns does Selke serve?
faqs.a: We serve Mooresville, Statesville, Troutman, and the surrounding Iredell County communities, including Lake Norman lakefront neighborhoods.

faqs.q: What pests are most common in Iredell County?
faqs.a: The most common pest problems in Iredell County are mosquitoes near Lake Norman, ticks on wooded and rural properties, fire ants, ants and spiders around foundations, and rodents seeking shelter in cooler months.

counties.name: Cabarrus County
counties.summary: Selke Pest Control provides residential general pest control, mosquito control, flea and tick control, and rodent control in Cabarrus County, North Carolina, with dedicated service in Concord.
counties.geography: Cabarrus County sits just northeast of Charlotte and is one of the fastest-growing counties in North Carolina. The Rocky River, Coddle Creek, and Irish Buffalo Creek wind through the county, and new subdivisions are being built on former farmland and wooded tracts. Disturbed soil favors fire ants, creek buffers favor mosquitoes and ticks, and the transition from farmland to housing pushes mice and rats into new homes.
pests: Mosquitoes along the Rocky River and creek greenways
Fire ants in new-construction yards
Ticks on wooded lot lines and open space
Ants and spiders around slab and crawl-space foundations
Rodents displaced by ongoing development

faqs.q: Does Selke Pest Control serve Cabarrus County?
faqs.a: Yes. We serve residential homes in Cabarrus County, including Concord and nearby communities. Call 704-728-0204 to confirm availability for your address.

faqs.q: Why are fire ants so common in Cabarrus County?
faqs.a: Rapid residential construction across Cabarrus County disturbs soil and creates open, sunny lawns, which are ideal conditions for fire ant colonies to establish and spread.

faqs.q: Does Selke offer mosquito control in Concord and Cabarrus County?
faqs.a: Yes. Selke Pest Control provides seasonal mosquito barrier treatments for Concord and Cabarrus County homes, typically from spring through fall.

counties.name: Rowan County

Barns, outbuildings, hay storage, livestock water, and tree lines create year-round habitat for rodents, ticks, stinging insects, and mosquitoes that are different from the pest pressure in suburban subdivisions.

Mice and rats around barns, feed, and outbuildings

faqs.q: Can Selke treat large rural properties in Mount Ulla?
